method: M1's script (the evaluate_script body behind wgsl-compile-all.json, taken from the session transcript), run through execute/async: a fresh device, every other WGSL module of the app compiled with createShaderModule inside a validation and an internal error scope, then getCompilationInfo. Changes forced by Safari, which has no subgroups feature: the device is requested without features, and cull is counted as the engine builds it in Safari, prepareShaderSource(cull, false); M1's two subgroup variants go to `extra`, next to the modules nothing imports. As in M1, `results` builds no pipeline (M1: "Pipelines are exercised by the harness tabs (M2)"); the pipelines M1 built with the two validators (19 primitive, 4 sort) are in wgsl-validation-safari.json. Added beyond M1, `pipelines`: the pipelines of the three modules whose harness checks read no pixel, built by the engine code inside the same two error scopes: ParticleSystem.buildSimulate and buildRender (the calls of the renderer and of the particle hot-reload, with the canvas format) and DebugLinePass.setup (LineBatchPass, the debug-line pipeline of the overlays). Nothing is drawn.

comparisonWithChrome.summary: The 15 modules the engine loads in Safari compile with no message and empty scopes, as their 15 counterparts in Chrome. Chrome counted 17: its other two are cull's subgroup variants, which the engine never builds without the 'subgroups' feature and which Safari rejects ('enable subgroups;': "Expected 'clip_distances', 'f16', or 'primitive_index'"). Every module has the source length it had in Chrome except bloom (7664 against 7099: bloom.wgsl changed in db55fed, the F4 fix, after M1). Not counted in either browser: prefix-sum, which Chrome compiles with its directive and Safari rejects at the same directive, and basic-binding-array, which fails in both with a different message (binding_array is not available).
